authority: User Messages 20 and 23 (free tools and freely licensed anatomy may be downloaded and used: pinned, vendored with licence files and credits, documented derivatives, raw packets untouched) and Message 1 ("No invisible ... body parts"), Message 18 (anatomical realism); the lead's task for builder AN (the large muscles the body packets lack, BodyParts3D 4.0 first, Z-Anatomy where BodyParts3D has none, the face packet's source and registration).
source_order: Every muscle was looked up first in the BodyParts3D 4.0 element list (isa_element_parts.txt of the official archive); a BodyParts3D file was taken whenever one exists. Z-Anatomy (the face packet's pinned file) was used only for the muscles with no BodyParts3D 4.0 file: latissimus dorsi, rectus abdominis, internal oblique, transversus abdominis, quadratus lumborum, longus colli, extensor digitorum brevis and flexor hallucis brevis.

licence_check.required_attribution: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science licensed under CC Attribution 4.0 International

bodyparts3d.method: HTTP range requests against the official archive only (serial, 1.5 s apart, no retries, same User-Agent naming the project): HEAD for identity (ETag and size must equal the recorded ones), the end of central directory, the central directory (its sha256 must equal the recorded one), then each member's local header and compressed bytes; raw-deflate decompressed; ZIP CRC32 and uncompressed size must equal the central directory's; then sha256. The same route builder FA used for packets/bodyparts3d-head-r1. Script: acquire_bp3d.py (pure Python standard library).
bodyparts3d.change: none: every FJ*.obj is the byte-exact decompressed archive member (CRC32, size and sha256 checked)
bodyparts3d.header_checks: each file's embedded File ID equals its element id, Compatibility version is 4.0, its English name is exactly "<side> <muscle>", its Concept ID is in the element list rows of that file, and its header bounds match its vertices within 1 mm (right-side files up to 0.48 mm, as in the full-body packet)

z_anatomy.same_as_face_packet: yes: the same commit, file, byte count and sha256 as packets/face-muscles-r1 (ACQUISITION-RECORD.json, SOURCES.json)
z_anatomy.licence_files_note: copied unchanged into LICENSES/ as Z-Anatomy-License.txt, Z-Anatomy-Model-Notice.txt, Z-Anatomy-Authors-and-Notice.txt, Z-Anatomy-Export-Readme.txt

conversion.tools: fbxread.py (a minimal binary FBX 7.x reader written for this packet: nodes, properties, zlib arrays; Python standard library only, no third-party code), zscene.py (scene graph: FBX Lcl translation / rotation (XYZ Euler) / scaling per node, parent chain, no pivots, as the face packet), zconvert.py (OBJ writer). No Blender or other tool was needed.
conversion.route: p_out = s * R * (W_node * p_src) + t with the face packet's recorded similarity (scale 9.86027892397196, rotation R, translation t in mm; the face packet's ACQUISITION-RECORD), polygons fan-triangulated, winding reversed for mirrored (negative determinant) nodes, unreferenced vertices dropped in source order, coordinates written with four decimals (mm).
conversion.face_packet_reproduction: zconvert.py --check-face: all 54 face-packet OBJ files reproduced line for line from the FBX (54 identical, 0 different), so this is exactly the face packet's route and transform.

frame_registration_check.method: regcheck.py: each Z-Anatomy object converted with the face similarity is compared with the SAME structure in BodyParts3D 4.0 (exact point-to-triangle distances, up to 1500 sampled vertices; mean offset = BodyParts3D minus Z-Anatomy, mm, +x subject left, +y posterior, +z superior). Different atlases model some structures differently (the trapezius parts are cut differently: the large values there are a segmentation difference, not a misplacement).

trunk_neck_hip_leg_pairs.zanatomy_object: Clavicular head of pectoralis major muscle.r
Sternocostal head of pectoralis major muscle.r

frame_registration_check.summary: Front and side of the trunk: external oblique 2.4 / 3.2 mm median (right / left), pectoralis major 2.5 to 3.8, serratus anterior 4.4, pectoralis minor 1.3; low back: iliocostalis lumborum 2.0 / 2.4, longissimus thoracis 4.5 / 4.7, serratus posterior inferior 4.0; neck: sternocleidomastoid 1.5, scalenus anterior 1.4, splenius capitis 3.9; hip and thigh: adductor longus 2.2, gluteus maximus 4.2, psoas 4.0, rectus femoris 4.1, piriformis 4.9; deep upper back 8 to 11 (semispinalis, rhomboid major, serratus posterior superior; Z-Anatomy lies 7 to 11 mm posterior); lower leg 8.6 to 12 (tibialis anterior, soleus, fibularis longus); feet about 28 to 30 mm before the per-foot correction. The Z-Anatomy files in this packet are trunk, neck and foot muscles; the deep upper back was NOT taken from Z-Anatomy (its muscles there have BodyParts3D files), and multifidus was left out because of that offset.

foot_refinement.why: after the face similarity the Z-Anatomy foot lies about 28 to 30 mm from the BodyParts3D foot (median), mostly too low: a scale error grows with the distance from the head, where the similarity was fitted.
foot_refinement.method: footrigid.py: per foot, a rigid correction (rotation + translation, no scale) by trimmed (90 %) point-to-surface ICP, Horn's closed-form absolute orientation, against the SAME two structures in BodyParts3D 4.0 (extensor hallucis brevis FJ1407 / FJ1407M and flexor digitorum brevis FJ1413 / FJ1413M); applied after the similarity to the three Z-Anatomy foot objects of that side (extensor digitorum brevis, the two heads of flexor hallucis brevis).

rejected_first_try.why_rejected: residuals stayed 5.2 / 2.0 mm median with 11 to 15 mm at the 90th percentile; the rigid fit brings them to about 0.9 / 0.7 mm median and 4.5 / 1.7 mm at the 90th percentile

frame_registration_check.bodyparts3d_files: unchanged archive coordinates: they are in this body's own frame by construction (the full-body packet is the same archive).

duplicates: No element id here is in inputs/FULLBODY-MESH-MANIFEST.json, inputs/MESH-MANIFEST.json, packets/face-muscles-r1 or packets/bodyparts3d-head-r1 (another branch; its ten files are cranium and eye layers); the loader also refuses a repeated id. FJ1532 (right levator scapulae) is taken alone because its left twin FJ1532M is already in the left-arm packet (shoulder girdle stream). No structure is drawn twice: the Z-Anatomy muscles have no BodyParts3D 4.0 file.
laterality: Every file's name side equals the side of its vertex centroid (x < 0 right, x > 0 left); files whose share of vertices on the named side is below 0.97 are listed in the manifest's source_anomalies (midline muscles such as spinalis thoracis, splenius capitis, serratus posterior inferior and the left latissimus dorsi, whose origins reach the spinous processes) and kept unchanged.
not_included: Muscles still not drawn anywhere in the game: multifidus and the rotatores (Z-Anatomy only; its deep upper back sits about 8 to 11 mm behind the BodyParts3D deep back, see ACQUISITION-RECORD.json, so it would cut into the BodyParts3D columns without a regional fit), the interspinales and intertransversarii, the suboccipital muscles, subclavius, the small sole muscles other than flexor digitorum brevis, abductor hallucis and flexor hallucis brevis (quadratus plantae, lumbricals, interossei, adductor hallucis, abductor and flexor digiti minimi of the foot), the pelvic floor, the diaphragm and the intercostals.
game_display_processing: Not part of the files: in the game (ns-body) the muscles take the Body Worlds stack levels of BODY_STACK_PACKET, the display fill, and the BodyParts3D external oblique's tendon sheet in front of rectus abdominis (and the obliques' laminae there) is not drawn (openRectusSheath, the sheath opened as in a dissection). All of this happens in browser memory only.
tools_and_scripts: acquire_bp3d.py, fbxread.py, zscene.py, zconvert.py, regcheck.py, footrigid.py, footfit.py, build_packet.py, write_manifest.py, write_record.py: Python 3 standard library only, written for this packet, run offline (except the downloads named above), pinned to one CPU.
